items.title: An ergodic symmetric interval exchange transformation whose middle point lies in a connection has minus one as an eigenvalue
items.author: Przemyslaw Berk; Frank Trujillo
items.work: Ergodic properties of infinite extension of symmetric interval exchange transformations
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled corollary at source lines 893-895: if an ergodic symmetric interval exchange transformation has its middle point inside a connection, then minus one is an eigenvalue of the associated Koopman operator. The proof (source lines 897-902) builds the eigenfunction rather than deducing the eigenvalue abstractly, and every step it needs is outside the statement: a symmetric subinterval avoiding all connections has to be selected, the description of the centres of the induced transformation has to be converted into the statement that all Rokhlin towers have even height, and only then can the level-wise sign function be defined and recognised as an eigenfunction.
